summary: The Flight Deck map can now show live rain, wind and turbulence, a solar night side, a configurable own-aircraft symbol and a 3D recorded track, all moving smoothly with the map.
releaseNotes: The Flight Deck map gains optional animated RainViewer radar, Open-Meteo wind streamlines and a smoothed turbulence layer, each switched on from Map settings.
The aircraft you are flying now has its own colour, size, halo and trail width, while traffic keeps its own styling.
A 3D recorded-track view shows the flight in perspective: left-drag turns it, right-drag tilts it, and the latest point carries an aircraft marker.
The map's day/night layer is a solar-elevation mask with a smooth twilight band, rebuilt as the map moves instead of lagging behind a pan.
The route ahead starts at the aircraft while the flown path stays behind it, and the 3D view uses the same recorded track as the map.
Weather requests are cached and refreshed on a timer, so radar frames and model fields stay smooth without repeated calls on every frame.
Turbulence is drawn as an interpolated amber-to-red field instead of separate blobs, and wind is drawn as moving streamlines instead of arrows.
Panning with the day/night layer on no longer leaves a diagonal night wedge, because the mask follows the current map view.
A route saved before procedure geometry was versioned now re-resolves its departure instead of keeping the old runway turn.
The 3D view no longer opens a browser context menu on right-drag or changes pitch when the pointer only pans.
Turning off the own trail or changing its width no longer affects traffic trails or traffic colours.
Radar, wind and turbulence are built from cached, coarse rasters that update only when the map view or refresh timer changes.
The day/night mask rebuilds in the same frame as a pan, keeping map movement at a steady frame rate.
Map settings now has an Own aircraft & trail card with a colour picker, size and trail-width sliders, halo and trail switches, and a reset action.
Map layers are grouped in the Map settings panel, with short notes on the weather sources and what they do not replace.
Stored routes from earlier builds are upgraded in place, so no saved flight plan needs to be re-created.
The weather layers need a network connection to RainViewer and Open-Meteo; the rest of the map works without them.
Rain, wind and turbulence are planning aids, not PIREPs, SIGMETs or official weather.
